title: Frontier Safety Frameworks — RSP, PF, FSF

questions.question: What common design pattern appears in the LABS table for Anthropic, OpenAI, and DeepMind?
options: A single shared numeric benchmark and identical names
No published thresholds or external evaluation requirements
Tiered capability thresholds, domain-specific risk triggers, and safeguards that activate at higher capability
A single privacy law replacing model evaluations
questions.explanation: The code prints different vocabularies—ASL, Low/Medium/High/Critical, and CCL—but each maps capability evidence to a higher-risk response. Structural alignment does not mean identical cutoffs.

questions.question: Why is Anthropic's ASL ladder compared with biosafety levels?
options: Both are tokenization standards
ASL is a legal penalty schedule copied verbatim from BSL
Biosafety levels measure model helpfulness
Both use increasing levels to connect capability or hazard evidence with increasingly strict controls
questions.explanation: The analogy is operational: a level is a threshold for safeguards, not a claim that AI and biological hazards are identical. The lesson's table lists ASL-3 as the cited CBRN activation point.

questions.question: Which OpenAI Preparedness Framework criterion captures harm that happens quickly or cannot be undone?
options: Instantaneous-or-irremediable
Net-new
Measurable
Capability-neutral
questions.explanation: Instantaneous-or-irremediable is a harm characteristic: delayed intervention cannot reliably reverse the outcome. It is distinct from whether a capability is novel or whether it can be measured.

questions.question: What is a competitor-adjustment clause in the framework comparison?
options: A license discount for models that pass a benchmark
A provision that may reduce safeguards when peer labs ship without comparable requirements
A rule requiring every lab to use the same CBRN test
A replacement for a safety case with a model card
questions.explanation: The table marks such a clause in all three entries. It creates a governance race-to-the-bottom risk: external competitive pressure can weaken a commitment that was intended to track capability.

questions.question: Which three pillars does the lesson use to structure a frontier safety case?
options: Speed, accuracy, and cost
Helpful, honest, and harmless
Monitoring, illegibility, and incapability
Inner, outer, and mesa alignment
questions.explanation: A safety case can argue that dangerous behaviour is observable, difficult to elicit or interpret, or unavailable to the model. These are complementary claims, not interchangeable labels for alignment theory.

questions.question: What can be concluded from structural agreement across ASL, PF, and CCL?
options: The labs use identical evaluations and numeric cutoffs
The frameworks are unrelated because their names differ
A competitor-adjustment clause proves every model is safe
They converge on tiered capability thresholds and safety cases, while their terminology and criteria remain distinct
questions.explanation: The printed rows share the architecture of thresholds, CBRN/AI-R&D triggers, adjustment clauses, and safety-case artifacts. They do not establish equivalence of tests or guarantee that safeguards work.
